# Multi-Level Implementation Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)

> **Companion design document**. This document is a companion to
> [RFC-039 Compiler Architecture Restructuring](../../rfc/accepted/039-compiler-architecture.md). It
> expands the RFC's phase sequence into **three levels of independently committable and
> independently verifiable tasks**.
>
> RFC-039 is the sole authority for phase ordering and acceptance gates. This document is
> responsible only for breaking the work down into an executable granularity and recording conflicts
> that remain undecided.

## Purpose and Scope

| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Level 1** | 11 (P0–P10)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Phases, corresponding one-to-one with RFC-039's phase sequence                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |

**Reserved gaps (not reclaimed)**: P4 has no `4.7`/`4.8`, and P8 has no `8.1`. None of these three
has had a corresponding entry since the WBS was established: throughout this document's history, the
three headings `**4.7` / `**4.8` / `**8.1` have had zero matches (verifiable with
`git log -S'**4.7' -- docs/src/dev/architecture/09-execution-wbs.md`), and there are no
repository-wide references. `8.1` corresponds precisely to phase 1 of `05` (test revival and
completion). That phase was split into P1 (`1.1`–`1.3`) and `8.8`; therefore, P8's numbering is
aligned with its phase numbers: phase 0 → `8.0`, phase 2 → `8.2`, and so forth.

**Covered here**: task decomposition, dependencies, parallelization groups, and binding of
acceptance criteria.

**Not covered here**: the design rationale for tasks (see `02`–`08`) or the rationale for phase
ordering (see RFC-039).

**Registration convention (effective 2026-10-12)**: newly registered Level 2/Level 3 rows **must
contain two fields**—**"Owning phase"** (the P to which the task truly belongs, which may differ
from the containing section) and **"Blocks the main line?"**. `Registered, awaiting scheduling` is
no longer the default state; an unmarked task is deemed **not schedulable**. Numbers must be
**unique throughout the document** (cross-track tasks use their track number, such as `029g.x`, and
must not occupy an `N.x` number). **Checkoff/completion registration is based on "task id + evidence
(gate values, run id, issue number, file:line)"**, not commit numbers—`pull --rebase` rewrites local
hashes, so hard-coded numbers inevitably become invalid (2026-10-13 example:
`94ad03ce4`→`631eb3e3c`). Look up commit numbers with `git log`.

## Current State: Gaps Found During Decomposition

While consolidating the "Implementation Highlights" from eight documents into the table below,
**five hard gaps in the documentation system itself** were found. All have now converged:

| #   | Gap                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Resolution                                                                                                                                                  |
| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| G1  | **P5 had no implementation steps whatsoever.** RFC defined P5 (splitting the checker) and its acceptance criterion (C1 zero-diff), but none of the seven documents described how to perform that split; the directory tree in `01-routing.md` mentioned `annotations.rs` once, the only mention in the entire batch.                                                                  | P5's steps are supplied here (see below).                                                                                                                   |
| G2  | **The `include!` conversion had three possible owners and no implementation.** RFC assigned it to P4; `02` assigned the reference to itself; `06` also listed it under S7. However, `02`'s change list (6 additions + 20 modifications) **did not include `semantic_tokens.rs`**.                                                                                                     | The implementation steps belong in §P5 5.1 of this document (after P4 is complete); references in RFC and `06` now point here.                              |
| G3  | **Three coexisting lists of CI scripts.** `RFC` lists four `scripts/ci/*.py` scripts; `01` lists four scripts + 1 `cargo test`; `07` separately lists four checks (all with different names); `04` additionally requires `check-synth-boundary.py`. After deduplication, there are **at least 9 new scripts and no unified list**; `check-obligations.py` is owned by both P4 and P9. | The unified list appears in §P9 of this document (11 scripts, each owned by one phase); all other documents refer to this table.                            |
| G4  | **Conflict over the life of `precedence_inline.rs`.** `06` counts it among the "1005 lines that must be revived", while B6 in the same document says it "must be deleted together with the `Precedence` enum"; `05` argues for deletion.                                                                                                                                              | **Revive in P1, delete with Pratt in P8** (decision registration C1)—first restore CI coverage, then delete the file in 8.6 together with the Pratt ladder. |
| G5  | **Conflicting statements of the L2 objective.** RFC and the directory index state "grammar-driven syntax", whereas `05` self-assesses: "**We did not adopt true grammar-driven parsing (LALRPOP); we only implemented declarative table lookup**."                                                                                                                                    | Converged on **full LALRPOP grammar-driven parsing** (`05` §Syntax: Full Grammar-Driven Parsing); the G7/G8 acceptance gates enforce that commitment.       |

## Target Design: Phase Sequence

```
P0  仓库维护机制与代码放置规程     08        ← 新增，先立规矩
P1  复活孤儿测试并修缺陷           06 §S1
P2  建立等价性判据基线             07 全部
P3  修正确性漏洞（最小方案）        02 §S3-漏洞半部
P4  阶段契约与统一 Driver          02
P5  checker 文件内拆分             02 + 本文补齐
P6  类型表示单一化                 03
P7  中间表示 SSA 化                04      } 可并行
P8  前端范式变更                   05      }
P9  防反弹门禁（含统一脚本清单）     01 §防反弹 + 08 §可机检规则
P10 其余清理与状态修正             06 §S2/S3/S4/S5/S6
```

**Rationale for adding P0**: the three prohibitions—no ad hoc invention, no endless filling, and no
patching where a refactor is required—constrain every action in P1–P10. The rules must be
established before implementation begins; otherwise, while P1 revives tests, it will already be
adding `mod` declarations to `tests/mod.rs`, which is precisely the source of the G4 conflict.

> **There is no size-baseline task.** The 2026-10-03 decision canceled every line-count / size gate.
> Size problems are instead addressed through separation of responsibilities (see `08` Prohibition 2
> criterion A, which requires human judgment). **0.2.1 is this phase's core acceptance criterion**:
> if the gate cannot report the known parallel representations, the criterion design is wrong and
> the gate is a false gate.

> **Semantic-fix routing (D59, user decision on 2026-10-11)**: if this track or a later phase
> discovers a defect where "the old behavior did not count as success"—**A silent failure / B silent
> mismatch / C undefined behavior and resource loss** (crash, stack exhaustion, or silently
> incorrect results)—it **may be fixed along with the refactor**, but all four requirements are
> mandatory: ① red first, then green (the red criterion must already exist and actually be red); ②
> do not change the externally observable behavior of programs that previously compiled successfully
> and ran correctly (they must not start failing, and their existing diagnostic codes/text/exit
> codes must not be removed or changed); ③ register it in the same commit (this row identifies the
> error type + a revision note for that phase + the PR's required "Error type" field); ④ regenerate
> the baseline in the same commit + manually review the diff. **D user-visible semantics / E
> external contract tables / F RFC-level design changes must still receive a user decision first.**
> See [07 §Routing Criteria for Semantic Fixes](07-equivalence-oracle.md) for the expanded criteria
> and A–F whitelist; **the "default super-refactor followed by retrospective registration" approach
> is not accepted** (the rationale is in RFC-039 D59: without a red criterion, fixes cannot be
> distinguished from regressions, and this conflicts with both "there is no C5′" and "no relaxation
> of any kind").

      2026-10-24, issue [#501](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/501); source =
      batch-review finding F4 from 4.10 round 2; the **parenthesized function type in the return
      position** has the wrong nesting level during decomposition—`g: () -> ((x: Int) -> Int) = inc`
      reports E1012 and expects `int64` (the annotation was read as **curried**, meaning "one value
      parameter, returning Int"), while `g: () -> ((x: Int) -> Int) = () => { return inc }` expects
      `fn(int64)->int64` but finds the lambda's **overall** type (`fn() -> fn(int64)->int64`); the
      two paths give **mutually contradictory expectations** for the same annotation, so a function
      "declaring a function return type" **has no valid annotation form at all** (removing the
      annotation makes it pass). **The annotation itself parses correctly** (the parser was ruled
      out by measurement). **Owning phase: P3; Blocks the main line: No**)

### External Track RFC-029g: Remove `pub` and Auto-Binding (External Track / #399 — Ordering Constraint D56)

Source: [RFC-029g](../../rfc/accepted/029g-remove-pub-and-auto-bind.md) (accepted on 2026-10-02,
implementation not started), [#399](https://github.com/ChenXu233/YaoXiang/issues/399). **This track
is not a design item of the refactor itself; it is a specification-compliance deletion forced by an
ordering constraint**, and is separate from P10 S5 ("reduce the visibility of `pub` items", i.e.
narrowing Rust's `pub(crate)`).

**Why it must be completed before P4 as a whole**: 029g's deletion surface overlaps the rewrite
surfaces of four refactor phases. Reversing the order means repeating the same deletions and
baseline updates on the new grammar / new checker layout / new SSA IR.

**Acceptance (behavioral changes, red criterion first)**:

1. **Red first, then green**: each of the two behavioral changes must first have a red criterion
   before code changes—① `pub` changes from "silently accepted" to a parse error; ② unreferenced
   top-level bindings in Lib/Script roles newly report W1001 (previously `pub` items were absolutely
   exempt).
2. **The test count must not decrease**: when deleting the `exempt_pub` cases in
   `typecheck/passes/tests/dead_code.rs` and the `is_pub` fixture, equivalent new cases must replace
   them.
3. **Baseline in the same commit**: diagnostic-set changes (new parse error + new W1001) ⇒ update
   the corpus-differential baseline (`tests/baselines/corpus-parity.jsonl`) and CHANGELOG in the
   same commit; IR snapshots are expected to have zero diff, and any non-zero diff must be
   explained.
4. **Independent revert unit**: the entire batch occupies one commit group and must not be mixed
   with other phases (DoD 6).
5. `cargo test` / `clippy -D warnings` / `python scripts/rfc/check_tracking.py` all green.

**Ordering**: overlaps with 3.4 in files (`checker.rs`, `environment.rs`) ⇒ the two must be serial
and cannot run in parallel; **the whole track precedes P4** (RFC-039 D56). The 029g track does not
depend on 3.4; the implementer may choose which to do first based on the context at hand.

> main-chain/constraint rows) was merged into `97071c81b` together with RFC-039's D56 during the
> parallel-flow workspace cleanup. That commit's message records "3.4 addendum registration +
> D57/D58 decision recording" and does not mention this track. History is not rewritten; it is
> recorded in place following the existing convention (the `d5b18390` precedent, see the P2 landing
> note), as a retrospective bisection basis.

|                             | 5.2.2 Close the refinement entry point around "`&self` + return diagnostics", **without leaving `impl`**: `collect_refined_binding_checks` (now `checker/refinement.rs`, `pub(super)`) no longer implicitly writes to the error channel through `&mut self`; the diagnostic set is returned to the caller, whose sole write point is in `check_module_impl` (`checker.rs`, symbol location). **Reason for not leaving `impl`**: the only field in this family is `self.env` (so leaving `impl` is technically feasible), but converting the entry point and traversal entirely to free functions would also relocate these call sites: `resolve_type_annotation` has 8 production sites (6 annotation paths + `refined_walk_stmt` + `collect_refined_var_names_in_stmt`), and `collect_param_refinements` has 2 production sites + 1 test, and would create a reverse dependency from the retained surface (signature collection) to refinement—the opposite of the coupling this step is intended to eliminate | 5.2.1        | C1 zero-diff; four **symbol criteria**: ① the signature contains no `&mut self` ② the function body contains zero `env.errors` ③ the **entry point's returned** diagnostics are written at exactly one caller site ④ the entry point still has exactly 1 site |

|                             | 5.3.2 **Keep `collect_used_in_type` (`pub(crate)`) as `pub(crate)` and under the `checker` module path**: it is a **shared-surface** function (consumed on both sides by `collect_function_signature` and `inference/statements.rs:16`), and 5.3.1 empirically **did not move it** ⇒ the "zero caller changes" criterion **was already satisfied**, so **do not add** a new `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` re-export. **Constraint retained**: if it is moved with the family in the future (into annotations or another later batch), `checker.rs` must add `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` so that the existing import remains byte-for-byte unchanged                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | 5.3.1        | **"Zero caller changes" is this step's hard acceptance criterion**: `git diff src/frontend/core/typecheck/inference/statements.rs` is empty                                                                                                                   |

**Hard constraint**: `collect_used_in_type` is used across modules by `inference/statements.rs:16`.
**If** the function is moved with the annotation family in the future, **then** `checker.rs` must
add `pub(crate) use annotations::*;` so that the existing import remains byte-for-byte unchanged;
5.3 empirically **did not move it**, so this batch added no re-export (the criterion was already
satisfied).

**Only split confirmed large blocks.** Do not split modules of only 200–400 lines—that increases
navigation cost, reduces cohesion, and yields no decoupling benefit. The remaining submodules
(signatures / type_defs / imports) are deferred until the files grow back to 1,500 lines.

### P9 Anti-Rebound Gates (Unified Script List — This Document Supplements the Original Gap G3)

Source: [01](01-routing.md) §Anti-Rebound Mechanism + [08](08-maintenance-mechanism.md)
§Machine-Checkable Rules

**This is the sole authoritative list of all CI scripts** (11 scripts). Scripts are connected to CI
at their "introduction phase"; scripts marked report-only become strict in P9 (change from "report"
to "fail")—existing violations (parallel representations, disambiguation aliases, etc.) must wait
until P6/P8 to be cleared; making the gates strict too early would leave CI permanently red and
encourage humans to bypass the gates, so when P9 makes them strict, they should be exactly green.

## Implementation Highlights: Dependencies and Parallelization

### Mandatory Serial Main Chain

`P0 → P1 → P2 → P3 → P3.5 → P4 → P5 → P6 → (P7 ∥ P8) → P9 → P10`

> **P3 stopgap path (decision on 2026-10-05)**: P3's prerequisites are narrowed to **2.3.2 + 2.4.1 +
> 2.4.3** (multi-file corpus layer + two red criteria). The rest of P2 (2.1 IR verifier, 2.2
> snapshots, 2.3.1/2.3.3 differential and performance baseline) may proceed in parallel with P3.
> Correctness defects must not be blocked by criterion-infrastructure construction; but **P4 must
> still wait for all of P2**—the unified Driver requires all three layers of criteria to be in
> place.

| Constraint                | Reason                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| P0 → P1                   | The three prohibitions constrain every P1 action (1.2.x is itself adding `mod` declarations to `mod.rs`)                                                                                                                                               |
| P1 → P2                   | Reviving tests changes the test count and corpus baseline                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| P2 (after narrowing) → P3 | Vulnerability criteria must be **written as red first** (2.4.1/2.4.3) + the multi-file corpus layer (2.3.2) must exist so that the red tests have somewhere to run                                                                                     |
| P3 → P4                   | Fix bugs before refactoring; reversing the order causes bugs to become fixed as "established behavior" in the phase table                                                                                                                              |
| P3.5 → P4                 | RFC-029g (#399)'s deletion surface covers the rewrite objects of P4 4.2.2 / P5 / P6 / P7 / P8 (see the list in §P3.5 of this document)—reversing the order means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, new checker layout, and new IR (D56) |
| P4 → P5                   | The `include!` conversion and checker split modify the same file                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| P5 → P6                   | Consecutive changes to the same file must be separated, otherwise a regression cannot be bisected                                                                                                                                                      |
| P6 → P7 / P8              | If type representations are not converged first, the new IR will grow into a third representation                                                                                                                                                      |
| P7/P8 → P9                | The 9.5 snapshot baseline and 9.3 `pub(crate)` leak count reach their final form only after P7/P8                                                                                                                                                      |

### Parallelization Groups

| Group                                  | Members                                                                            | Basis                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **A (the only one authorized by RFC)** | P7 ∥ P8                                                                            | Disjoint file sets: `ir.rs`/`ir_gen.rs`/`bytecode.rs`/`translator.rs` vs `lexer/*`/`parser/*`                                                                                                                                                         |
| B                                      | 1.2.1 ∥ 1.2.2 ∥ 1.2.3 ∥ 1.2.4                                                      | Each independently adds a `mod`, with file-by-file revert                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| C                                      | 2.1 ∥ 2.2 ∥ 2.3.1 ∥ 2.3.2 ∥ 2.4                                                    | The three criterion layers are independent                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| D                                      | 4.4 (proof-layer closeout) ∥ the entire P6 line                                    | `02` explicitly states that S5 "should proceed independently of S1-S4"                                                                                                                                                                                |
| E                                      | 4.2.5 ∥ 4.2.6 ∥ 4.2.8                                                              | All become mutually independent after 4.1 is complete                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| F                                      | 9.3 ∥ 9.9 ∥ 9.10 (the three scripts introduced in P0 may be developed in parallel) | The 9.5 snapshot baseline must be taken last                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| G                                      | S3 ∥ S4 ∥ S5                                                                       | Disjoint file sets (verified on 2026-10-05: S3 changes `docs/src/dev/design/check/` + `config.js`; S4 changes `docs/src/rfc/` + the `check_tracking.py` generator; S5 changes two `pub` sites in `src/frontend/core/typecheck/`; no pairwise overlap) |

**Cannot run in parallel (file overlap)**: P1(1.1.x) ∥ P8(8.0.x); 1.2.1 ∥ 8.3.2; 6.0 ∥ S2 (same
files in the B6/E5 batch); 4.3.2 ∥ 9.2 (already unified under P4); **3.4 ∥ P3.5** (`checker.rs` /
`environment.rs` are the same files—the external track's `pub` deletion batch and the silent-channel
fixes must be serial).

**New internal documentation constraint**: 6.0→6.1→6.2→6.3→6.4→6.5→6.6 is strictly serial;
7a→7b→7c→7d is strictly serial, and 7b's `Phi` arm must precede 7d.

## Key Decisions and Rationale

- **P0 is an independent phase rather than part of P9**—gates are "post-hoc checks"; rules are
  "prior judgment". P9's scripts cannot prevent "patching where a refactor was required"; only the
  D0–D4 review checklist can.
- **P9 is the sole authoritative list of CI scripts**—the original gap G3's three coexisting lists
  prevented convergence. This table merges them, with 11 scripts each owned by one phase and
  explicit report-only and strict-transition points.
- **P3.5 incorporates RFC-029g rather than leaving it as an "independent track to execute after the
  refactor"**—its deletion surface overlaps the rewrite surfaces of P4/P5/P6/P7/P8 (RFC-039 D56).
  Deferring it until after the refactor means repeating the same deletions on the new grammar, new
  checker layout, and new IR; this is the same lesson as incorporating `2315`/`2341` into 7e and RFC
  status correction into S4.
- **P5's steps are supplemented here rather than merged into P4**—P4 is already the largest
  single-point risk, and adding the checker split would exceed the rollback granularity.
- **5.3.2 uses "zero caller changes" as hard acceptance**—the split must be independently
  revertable.

## Known Limitations and Risks

- **1.3.x (fixing exposed defects) has no regression criterion**—it only says "fixed defects should
  not be rolled back" and lacks a requirement to record "what was fixed". **Execution convention**:
  every 1.3.x fix commit message must reference the fixed test name and defect description,
  providing a retrospective bisection basis.
- ~~**7b.1 granularity is too coarse**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: split into 7b.1a / 7b.1b as two
  exclusive commits under DoD 6.
- **8.2.1 granularity is too coarse**—approximately 89 references must be renamed, and missing one
  will **silently change associativity**.
- ~~**D17 / D20 have no corresponding Level 3 tasks**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: D17 became 7e.1, D20
  became 4.5.1/4.5.2; D32/D34 opcode reclamation was merged into 7e.1, while the deletion remains in
  P10 S6.
- ~~**The `2315` / `2341` data-loss defects were originally assigned to an "independent issue"**~~
  **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated as 7e.2 / 7e.3. The exception table (throw/try) is core
  language semantics and must not be left for later implementation.
- ~~**E2 (`lib.rs:568/582` `todo!()`) has no phase ownership**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: merged into
  P10 S2.
- ~~**F7 (opcode-gate extractor) ownership is ambiguous**~~ **Fixed (2026-10-05)**: incorporated
  into P10 S6's generation-time gate task.

| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| C1              | `precedence_inline.rs` is revived in P1 and deleted in P8                      | **Revive** (P1's prerequisite is reviving tests with real assertions); P8's 8.6 deletes the file together with Pratt                                 |
| C2              | The "grammar-driven" commitment vs table lookup                                | **Fully implemented**: use LALRPOP, see `05` "Syntax: Full Grammar-Driven Parsing"                                                                   |
| C3              | Conflict between C6 category definitions and S1 classification                 | **S1 belongs to C6** (revival does not require equivalence criteria, only regression tests); C6 is expanded to mean "pure deletion or pure revival"  |
| C4              | Whitelist for `test_release_plan_spans_consumed`                               | **No whitelist**; the difference set must be empty; if it cannot be empty, the `ReleasePlan` contract is defective → change it to `PlanId` (D20/D41) |
| C5              | Internal differences between the two `Aggregation` functions remain unverified | **P4's 4.2.7 makes this a mandatory verification item**, to be confirmed line by line during implementation                                          |
| C6              | The wasm playground fix requires P4's `ProgramKind`                            | **The wasm-path defect fix is merged into 4.2.8**; P3 handles only the three native entry points                                                     |
| C7              | Ownership of `method_def_ordinals`                                             | **Assigned to 04** (P7 batch c), see D21                                                                                                             |
| C8              | `upvalue_count` correction and the `.42` version number                        | **Fix + raise `VERSION` from 4 to 5** (the format header already has `MAGIC` + `VERSION` fields, `codegen/bytecode.rs:14-16`), see D17               |
